# Texture, grids and finish

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Grain, dither, halftone, pixel and glyph textures, grids and stepped cadence that give the picture a surface. 36 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Line-art pattern fills the end card

`dv-line-art-endcard-pattern` · logo and end card · accent · energy calm · launch, sting

Large thin outlines (2-3 px) of a motif in a lighter tint of the accent fill the end card behind the title and logo.

- **Build:** Recipe: an SVG line-art layer inside the end card's drift. Recipe: interpolate between a few hand-drawn key paths on a 24 f cycle, or offset each point by noise(i, f). Anatomy: Static line art, drifting with the card. Sound: None. Materials: The line art is alive: the outlines behind the end card keep morphing (tongues stretch, curl and change silhouette, 4-8 px of tip travel a frame) so the field flickers gently like a drawing of fire; stroke about 4 px at 1080p in a pale tint of the ground's hue at about 45 % contrast, round joins, no fill.
- **Materials:** The line art is alive: the outlines behind the end card keep morphing (tongues stretch, curl and change silhouette, 4-8 px of tip travel a frame) so the field flickers gently like a drawing of fire; stroke about 4 px at 1080p in a pale tint of the ground's hue at about 45 % contrast, round joins, no fill.
- **Timing:** Static.
- **Use when:** End cards on a full accent field.
- **Avoid when:** Motifs unrelated to the brand.

### Feathered edge mask

`tx-feathered-edge-mask` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy any · walkthrough, feature, loop, vertical

Lists, reels and overflowing lines dissolve into the stage at a soft edge instead of being cut by a hard crop, so content feels endless and the eye stays in the clear middle.

- **Build:** Put the moving content inside a fixed container with `maskImage` (and `WebkitMaskImage`) set to `linear-gradient(to bottom, transparent 0%, #000 14%, #000 86%, transparent 100%)`, so rows enter and leave by fading into the stage; move the content inside by transform only, with inertia() for a flicked reel or E.glide for single steps. For a typed line that must follow its caret, use a left feather `linear-gradient(to right, transparent 0, #000 140px)` on the line's box and slide the text left by exactly its overflow each frame. Size the feather at 10-15% of the container (120-160 px at 1080p): shorter reads as a crop, longer greys out readable rows.
- **Timing:** Feather 10-15% of the container; list steps 26-40 f on E.glide, or inertia(f, s, 30-60, 0.89) for a proof reel; text under the mask at most 20 px/f while it must read; the mask itself never moves.
- **Use when:** Endless-feeling lists, proof reels, logs, chats, card stacks, and type that overflows its line as it is typed.
- **Avoid when:** Content that must be read right at the container edge; a hard-cropped bento look; as a full-frame vignette (that is lighting, not a mask).

### Fog floor

`tx-fog-floor` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The bottom fifth of the frame lightens toward the stage's brightest tone, as if the UI hovers above a softly lit floor that receding planes can sink into.

- **Build:** Bake a full-frame RGBA PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py: linear, angle 0 (bottom to top), stops [floor tone at 0, floor tone at alpha 0.6 at 0.12, transparent at 0.22], where the floor tone is a near-white just above the stage in the same hue (OKLCH L about 0.98). Layer it above the background and below the UI. When a panel tilts back into depth (perspective 2000-2400 px, transformOrigin at its bottom edge, rotateX 0 to 60 degrees over 30-40 f on E.in), render a second copy of the fog above that panel so it dissolves into the floor, and take the panel's opacity to 0 on E.in over the last 12 f. On an ink stage the floor tone is C.ink raised OKLCH 0.04.
- **Timing:** The floor band is 22% of frame height and fixed to the stage; tilt-backs 30-40 f on E.in with the fade over their last 12 f.
- **Use when:** Light or pastel stages with 3D tilt-backs, lifts and recedes; any film that wants a horizon without drawing a floor.
- **Avoid when:** Flat, front-on UI with no depth moves; dark stages that already have a light pool; vertical frames where captions sit in the bottom fifth.

### Global frame-keyed grain

`tx-global-grain` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy any · any

A fine, even grain sits over the whole film at one strength, breaking banding in soft ramps and blurred plates and giving flat colour fields a tactile surface.

- **Build:** Bake 8 seeded noise tiles offline (512x512 PNG, numpy gaussian noise with sigma about 90 levels, centred on the stage's own luma so the stage is not lifted); never Math.random or an animated feTurbulence. Add one full-frame top layer: a div with the tile as backgroundImage, normal blend at opacity 0.015-0.02, tile index Math.floor(fd(frame) / 2) % 8, and backgroundPosition offset by Math.floor(rand(index) x 512) px in x and y so the repeat never shows. Keep the same strength from the first frame to the last (never per scene), verify on a flat mid-grey crop (sigma about 1.5-2 code levels) and confirm forensics.py reports no smear. Grain does not replace baked dither: soft gradients still ship as dithered PNGs from scripts/dither-gradient.py.
- **Timing:** New tile every 2 f; constant strength (sigma ~1-2.3 code levels) for the whole film; no fades and no per-scene changes.
- **Use when:** Films with large flat or saturated colour fields, soft lighting ramps, blurred photo plates, or a tactile, filmic brand.
- **Avoid when:** Crisp, clinical UI films where any texture reads as dirt; when the strength would have to change between scenes; as a fix for banding that dithered PNGs should solve.

### Gobo-lit studio backdrop

`tx-gobo-studio-shadows` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

The UI floats over an off-white studio backdrop crossed by huge, very soft diagonal shadows, like window light through leaves, so flat screens feel photographed.

- **Build:** Stage C.paper (a cool off-white around #F7F7F7). Bake 3-5 shadow bands as RGBA PNGs at 120% of frame size with scripts/dither-gradient.py: linear gradients at 30-40 degrees, each going transparent to rgba(0,0,0,0.05-0.08) to transparent across 10-18% of the gradient line (the look of grey shapes blurred 100-150 px at 8-15% opacity, without the banding). Layer them above the stage and below the cards, and drift each along its own axis by A x sin(2 pi f / P + phi) with A = 40-80 px and P = 600-900 f, which keeps them under 0.5 px/f. Cards get `0 30px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.12)` and a 1 px C.line border.
- **Timing:** Band drift under 0.5 px/f on sines with 600-900 f periods and spread phases; present in every light shot of the act, unchanged between shots.
- **Use when:** Light-stage product films and walkthroughs that need depth and physicality without glass, colour or a 3D set.
- **Avoid when:** Dark stages; dense UI that fills the frame edge to edge; strictly flat graphic brands.

### Grain and print texture as the picture's finish

`dv-grain-and-print-texture` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy calm · any

Images carry visible grain, low-contrast highlights and soft focus while vector type stays razor sharp on top; white type over imagery carries a speckled, slightly broken print texture; a near-black stage carries a barely visible vertical micro-texture (3-5 % luma).

- **Build:** Recipe: cycled grain plates (seeded), a static speckle mask on the type, a baked micro-texture plate. Anatomy: Grain changing every frame; print speckle static; micro-texture most visible near the hero's glow. Sound: None.
- **Timing:** Grain every frame; others static.
- **Use when:** Editorial, image-led or dark tech films.
- **Avoid when:** Grain on UI text; texture strong enough to read.

### Grid cells switch on in a wave

`dv-grid-cell-wave` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy medium · any

Cells on a fixed grid switch on outward from a centre (each at one of a few random opacities), fade in as a radial wave and out centre-first, appear radially around a hub in a few steps, materialise in a diagonal wipe from a corner (duotone first, then colour), or multiply outward from one coloured cell.

- **Build:** Build: <CellWave at cols rows x y color shape="radial"|"diagonal"> (fx/Grids): cells switch on outward from origin at one of five seeded strengths (15-100 %), radial on E.buildIn over 23 f (on twos for the first 8 f) or diagonal (+1 f per column, +1.4 per row); fade={40} for a slow in-out, out={{ at }} leaves centre-first; render(cell) puts a thumbnail in each cell. Anatomy: Radial or diagonal threshold over a static grid; per-cell opacity from 5 levels (15-100 %); on twos for the first frames, then ones; cell 40 px on a 72 px pitch, or 60 px icons on a 95 px pitch. Sound: An onset on the wave; a sub on the gallery; a hit on the radial step. Materials: As cells multiply each holds the spreadsheet overflow mark in a dark tone; the clicked centre cell is the full accent and each ring of neighbours a lighter tint (five steps), so the wave reads as a heat map of distance; rows added every 5-6 f.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Grids.CellWave`
- **Materials:** As cells multiply each holds the spreadsheet overflow mark in a dark tone; the clicked centre cell is the full accent and each ring of neighbours a lighter tint (five steps), so the wave reads as a heat map of distance; rows added every 5-6 f.
- **Timing:** 23-75 f; each cell 40 f in-out; wave 20 f across; diagonal onset +1 f per column, +1.4 f per row.
- **Use when:** Openers, backgrounds that build, galleries of thousands, "it scales".
- **Avoid when:** Cells that move (they only switch).

### Hairline edge and key shadow

`tx-surface-edge-finish` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy any · any

Every floating surface gets a 1 px edge plus one soft key shadow on paper, or a top inner highlight on ink, so flat UI reads as a physical object in a lit space.

- **Build:** On paper: `boxShadow: '0 30px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.12)'` with a 1 px C.line border, optionally over a tight `0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.06)` contact shadow. On ink: no shadow, a C.ink2 fill (a luminance step from C.ink), a 1 px border at C.ink plus about OKLCH 0.06 lightness, and `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.08)` as the top highlight. Tie the finish to motion: when a card lifts (z 0 to 120 px) grow its shadow with the lift formulas (offset 0.1z, 0.22z; blur 3 + 0.06z; alpha 0.2 - 0.1 x min(1, z / 200)), and when a panel tilts toward camera raise the inset highlight from 0.08 to 0.12 with |tilt| / 15 degrees, so the edge catches light as it moves.
- **Timing:** Static finish; shadow and highlight follow the element's z and tilt every frame (lift 14 f on E.out, drop 10 f on E.in); highlight alpha changes by at most 0.04 over a tilt.
- **Use when:** Any floating card, panel, modal or window, in every format.
- **Avoid when:** Flush full-bleed UI or gutterless grids whose cells should merge into one canvas; anything tempting a glass panel or a coloured halo instead.

### Hairline layout grid as the ground

`dv-hairline-grid-ground` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy calm · any

A faint layout grid keeps empty space active: dashed grey cells on black that scale with the camera, a cutting-mat grid, hairlines a few percent darker than the page, guides with tiny square markers at intersections, grid paper with ruler ticks, a 1 px grid with small crosses at card corners, white rounded squares on near-white, a thin grid over photos; a wireframe grid of rectangles and nodes can pan and zoom.

- **Build:** Recipe: a static SVG pattern (or a baked plate) inside the camera transform; markers as small rects at chosen intersections. Anatomy: Cells 16-210 px; 1 px lines; optional heavier line every 5 cells, tick marks on edges, crosses or nodes at intersections; the grid either moves with the camera or stays fixed while the content moves (a fixed grid reads as the screen). Sound: None. Materials: The dashed grid can be barrel-curved like a lens (each point pushed out by 1 + 0.06 d^2 from the centre, about 12 px of sag at the frame edges) and the curve swims as the camera pushes; dashes 14 px with 8 px gaps, 1 px mid-grey, cells about 210 px.
- **Materials:** The dashed grid can be barrel-curved like a lens (each point pushed out by 1 + 0.06 d^2 from the centre, about 12 px of sag at the frame edges) and the curve swims as the camera pushes; dashes 14 px with 8 px gaps, 1 px mid-grey, cells about 210 px.
- **Timing:** Static; moves with the camera; a wireframe grid pans over 158 f.
- **Use when:** Product, tool and design films; any minimal ground that needs structure.
- **Avoid when:** Grids strong enough to read as content (keep lines 3-8 % off the ground).

### Low-luma photo plate

`tx-low-luma-photo-plate` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

A real photograph sits behind the UI or type, graded almost to black or thrown out of focus, adding context and tonal texture without stealing contrast from the copy.

- **Build:** A full-bleed <Img> overscanned 6% sits under everything, in one of two settings: (a) a sharp texture plate behind statements, `filter: grayscale(1) brightness(0.25) contrast(1.15)` tuned until its mean luma is 5-8%; (b) a defocused context plate behind a moving panel, pre-blurred offline at a 40 px radius (PIL GaussianBlur saved as PNG, so the browser never animates a blur; use src/fx/RackFocus.tsx if focus must change) with `brightness(0.6) saturate(0.4)`, translated at 0.3x the panel's or camera's translation for parallax. Keep plate hues neutral or cool, run the film's global grain over it so the dark ramps do not band, and separate the panel on top with a luminance step (C.ink2) and `inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.08)`. Plates may hard-cut on beats under a locked foreground whose pill or headline stays pixel-identical across the cut.
- **Timing:** A plate holds its shot (90-420 f) with 0.3x parallax or a 0.5-1.5 px/f drift; montage cuts under a locked foreground every 15-30 f on beats; never a fade on the plate.
- **Use when:** Dark-stage films that need real-world context (a desk, a city, a workspace) or a material, crafted feel behind sparse type or a floating panel.
- **Avoid when:** Light stages; a busy photo that stays above ~12% mean luma and fights the type; stock imagery unrelated to the product's world; decorative bokeh that names no job.

### One grade across mixed media

`tx-mixed-media-grade` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop

Desaturated photography, matte grey 3D, flat vector maps and line diagrams cut freely against each other without clashing, because every medium shares one dark value range and only the hero prop carries the accent.

- **Build:** Normalise each medium before it enters a shot: photos get `filter: grayscale(1) brightness(0.65) contrast(1.05)`; 3D or clay renders use matte grey materials (base around 40% grey, no coloured speculars) with C.accent on the hero prop only; vector maps fill land at C.ink plus OKLCH 0.03-0.04 lightness with 1.5 px borders at 15-25% white; line diagrams draw in white at 60-80% with the accent on the one active path. Check that every medium's mean luma lands within 8-25% and that nothing except the accent exceeds OKLCH chroma 0.03, then hard-cut or swap media inside a shot or grid cell on beats. The accent keeps the same single meaning in every medium.
- **Timing:** Swap media inside a shot or cell every 48-90 f, on beats; hard cuts between media need no transition because the value range already matches.
- **Use when:** Films that must combine photos, renders, maps, diagrams and UI, especially grid or bento layouts with several media on screen at once.
- **Avoid when:** Light, pastel or colourful brands; single-medium films; hero product photography that must keep its true colour.

### Stepped cadence for graphics

`tx-on-twos-cadence` · texture and finish · workhorse · energy medium · launch, update, feature, vertical · also `dv-stepped-cadence`

Graphics animate on 16 fps holds (or on twos) inside a smooth film while the camera stays smooth: crisp and hand-made, one held frame in three at 24 fps.

- **Build:** Wrap the graphics layer in <Stepped fps={16}> (on={2} for illustration); keep the camera transform outside it. Declare the range (declares() of Stepped) so blur sampling gives it one sample per frame.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Stepped.Stepped`, `fx/Stepped.useStepped`, `fx/Stepped.heldStats`
- **Timing:** 16 in 24: holds 1 of 3 frames; 16 in 60: holds 4, 4, 4, 3.
- **Use when:** Collages, illustration, markers, stickers, a build of pieces.
- **Avoid when:** Type reading or a camera move: those stay smooth.

### A fan of curves that keep vibrating like strings

`dv-string-curve-fan` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

From a hub (an app icon, a node) about sixteen curves fan out to the left and right and never freeze: their amplitudes swell and relax slowly, so they cross each other like vibrating strings or a moire; curves near the axis are saturated and thick, the outer ones thin and pale.

- **Build:** Recipe: 16-32 SVG paths recomputed each frame from closed-form amplitudes. Anatomy: Cubic curves from the hub's edge to the frame edge; stroke 2.5 px in the accent at the axis down to 1 px at 30 % outermost; amplitude oscillates 10-20 % on a 2-3 s period with a phase per curve; mirrored on the other side. Sound: VO only. Materials: Opacity and width fall linearly with the curve index; every curve converges exactly on the hub's edge.
- **Materials:** Opacity and width fall linearly with the curve index; every curve converges exactly on the hub's edge.
- **Timing:** Continuous for 3-6 s.
- **Use when:** Connection, sync, everything flowing into one; behind a hub while the VO speaks.
- **Avoid when:** Under text; next to another line texture.

### A patch of light carrying a lattice sweeps under the text

`dv-lattice-light-sweep` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

Before a send, a patch of pale light holding a fine white honeycomb lattice sweeps across the prompt box under the text; the lattice is only visible inside the light, so its edges dissolve, and the text and chips stay crisp on top.

- **Build:** Recipe: an SVG hex pattern masked by a moving radial gradient (a baked radial PNG as the mask) under the text layer, with a tint layer under the same mask. Anatomy: Light: a radial pale tint at about 70 % to transparent, about 420 x 300 px; hex cells about 55 px with 2 px white lines; travel about 30 px/f, decelerating. Sound: The send whoosh.
- **Timing:** 28 f.
- **Use when:** The send or run moment of a prompt box; a processing beat.
- **Avoid when:** Every send; dark text on a dark box.

### A portrait drawn in two digits under a rising gradient

`dv-glyph-portrait-gradient` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A picture is set as a terminal dump of monospace digits: one digit fills the ground, the other draws the figure in two-by-two blocks like pixel art, and a vertical gradient (white at the top, the accent at the bottom) rises through the glyphs until the card is accent on accent.

- **Build:** AsciiField with a bitmap source and a two-glyph ramp, its glyph layer used as a mask over a baked dithered gradient plate that rises by transform. Anatomy: Glyph cap about 14 px at 1080p, pitch about 17 px; the figure from a 1-bit bitmap on a grid of two-by-two glyph cells; fill = a gradient clipped to the glyphs whose top edge rises from 100 % to -20 % of the card; afterwards the glyphs are a pale tint of the accent on the accent. Sound: The card morph sits on a kick. Materials: Stops: near-white at the top edge, then the accent, then a deeper accent at the bottom; glyph colour after the rise = the accent mixed 25 % toward white.
- **Primitive:** `fx/GlyphField.GlyphField`
- **Materials:** Stops: near-white at the top edge, then the accent, then a deeper accent at the bottom; glyph colour after the rise = the accent mixed 25 % toward white.
- **Timing:** Gradient rise 50 f expo-out, texture holds 75 f.
- **Use when:** Developer, data and scraping products; the moment a card turns into what the machine sees.
- **Avoid when:** A film that already leans on a glyph texture elsewhere.

### Accent blocks jump between grid cells on kicks

`dv-grid-blocks-on-kicks` · texture and finish · accent · energy high · launch, feature

Solid accent blocks exactly one grid cell in size sit in the page grid forming steps and L shapes, and jump to new cells instantly, all together, on kicks.

- **Build:** HardStep positions from a table of cells indexed by the kick list. Anatomy: Blocks of one cell (192 px at 1080p); arrangements from a seeded table indexed by kick count. Sound: Kicks.
- **Primitive:** `fx/BlockStep`

### Design-tool guides that track a mask's bounding box

`dv-tracking-guides` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Behind a masked photo the faint lines are not a fixed grid: exactly two vertical and two horizontal hairlines sit on the edges of the mask's bounding box, extended across the frame, and they move with it as the mask breathes, like the guides of a design tool.

- **Build:** Recipe: four SVG lines placed from the mask's rect each frame. Anatomy: Lines 2 px at 1080p, about 10 luma off the ground, no blur; locked to the mask on every frame (no lag); they inherit the mask's breath and its contraction into the cut. Sound: A shutter click on the cut right after the contraction.
- **Timing:** As long as the mask: breath out 40 f, hold, in 10 f.
- **Use when:** A shape-led identity; design and layout products; any masked hero image.
- **Avoid when:** Busy grounds; together with a full grid.

### Dither-pixel patch licks up through outlines

`dv-dither-patch-sweep` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A patch of light dither pixels (small crosses) sweeps from bottom to top through a line drawing and dies out; the same burst repeats once.

- **Build:** Recipe: a seeded dither mask plate translated upward, multiplied with the line art. Recipe: a canvas clipped to the shape's path; per cell value = band(y + 6f) x (0.5 + 0.5 noise(x, y)); fillText the ramp glyph when the value is over 0.1. Anatomy: Coverage 0.9 -> 4.2 -> 0.8 %; bursts 21 f apart. Sound: A stab and a kick. Materials: A glyph patch licks up through a big shape and stays inside its outline: tiny light glyphs on a value ramp (dot < dash < equals < plus < x), denser in the middle and sparser at the edges, cells about 12 px at 1080p, colour a pale tint of the shape at 60-80 %; the band is about 45 % of the shape tall and scrolls about 6 px/f upward; each burst lives 32 f and repeats 52 f later.
- **Materials:** A glyph patch licks up through a big shape and stays inside its outline: tiny light glyphs on a value ramp (dot < dash < equals < plus < x), denser in the middle and sparser at the edges, cells about 12 px at 1080p, colour a pale tint of the shape at 60-80 %; the band is about 45 % of the shape tall and scrolls about 6 px/f upward; each burst lives 32 f and repeats 52 f later.
- **Timing:** 30 f per burst.
- **Use when:** End cards with line art; a "spark" without sparkles.
- **Avoid when:** Coverage above about 5 %.

### Dot grid seen only under wandering light

`dv-dot-grid-light-pools` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · any

A black stage carries a fine dot grid that is only visible where two or three very soft light pools drift, so the ground breathes with light.

- **Build:** LightField pools with the dot-grid plate as their mask (mix-blend multiply on a static grid layer). Anatomy: 12 px dot grid (luma 17-63) multiplied by the light pools (radius 300-500 px). Sound: None. Materials: Lights tint the grid: in a dark grid room the lines near each glowing object take that object's colour and brighten (spill radius 150-250 px, near lines at about 200 luma, far lines 40-60), so the grid reads as lit by the objects and the tints move with them.
- **Primitive:** `fx/LightField`
- **Materials:** Lights tint the grid: in a dark grid room the lines near each glowing object take that object's colour and brighten (spill radius 150-250 px, near lines at about 200 luma, far lines 40-60), so the grid reads as lit by the objects and the tints move with them.
- **Timing:** Continuous.
- **Use when:** Dark openers; tech films that want depth without objects.
- **Avoid when:** Pools that move fast (keep them slow, every 6-18 f of drift).

`dv-concentric-rings-ground` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · any

### Faint dot-matrix silhouette

`tx-dot-matrix-silhouette` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, vertical

Behind a claim, a barely visible field of dots forms a meaningful silhouette (a world map, a region, the product's own shape), adding literal context without competing with the type.

- **Build:** Precompute dot centres on a 20 px grid at 1080p, keeping only those inside a silhouette bitmap (a land mask, a region outline, the mark), and render them as one SVG of 13 px circles (or bake it to PNG). Fill the dots with the ground colour shifted about 4% in lightness, same hue (OKLCH 0.03-0.04: lighter on dark grounds, darker on light ones), and place the layer under the type. Keep it alive with a scale of lmix(1.00, 1.02, prog(f, s, e, E.linear)) across the shot or a translate under 1 px/f, and let it leave with the shot's cut rather than fading.
- **Timing:** Holds one shot of 80-100 f; scale 1.00 to 1.02 linear across it (well under 1 px/f); arrives and leaves on cuts, no fades.
- **Use when:** Claims about reach, coverage, location or scale, and any shot where a silhouette adds literal meaning behind the copy.
- **Avoid when:** Generic decoration with no meaning; contrast above ~6%, where it starts competing with the copy; small vertical frames where 13 px dots read as noise (scale the pitch up instead).

### Glyph-grid shock pulse

`tx-glyph-grid-pulse` · texture and finish · accent · energy high · launch, sting

On the film's biggest hit, the dark background flashes a grid of tiny monoline marks that bend outward from the impact like a shockwave, then settles back to a quiet grained field.

- **Build:** One SVG or canvas layer over the stage holds a grid of 36 px cells at 1080p, each with a 10 px monoline mark picked by rand(cellIndex) from plus, L, T and slash, stroked 1.5 px in white. With t = f - hit and pulse = hitPulse(t, 4, 3), each mark at distance d from the impact point gets opacity 0.6 x (1 - d / R) x pulse and a radial offset of 30 x pulse x (1 - d / R) px outward (R about 900 px), so the grid bulges like a tunnel and dies away. Play it once, on the payoff or the lockup's landing, with the hit sound on the hit frame.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep it strictly grid-locked so it reads as structure, not a burst: plus marks only, every cell on the grid with no scatter or random drift, opacity capped at 0.35, a single displacement ring, monochrome, and no streaks of light. The full look relies on particles; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** About 12-14 f visible, peaking 4 f after the hit (hitPulse(t, 4, 3)); 30 px radial push at peak; once per film.
- **Use when:** A digital or developer brand's payoff hit or lockup landing that needs a shockwave without colour or glow.
- **Avoid when:** Calm films; more than once per film; light stages; behind type that is still arriving.

### Ground made of vertical bars

`dv-fluted-bar-ground` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

The background is a field of flat vertical bars (about 100 px wide), each a single shade, so a soft glow reads as a stepped poster; or vertical stripes with soft light gradients like fluted glass.

- **Build:** Recipe: render the light field into a few bands of flat colour (posterised horizontally), moved by transform. Shader or canvas: x quantised to 16 bars, band = smoothstep on the distance to a tilted line that moves, colour from a ramp at the bar's centre; the bars have hard edges, so banding is not an issue. Anatomy: Bars quantise a smooth field into steps; the glow can spread, sweep and wander. Sound: None. Materials: The glow is a staircase, not a gradient: hard vertical bars, each one flat colour stepping from a warm deep tone through the accent to violet and black across the frame (about 16 bars), with a smooth fade to black vertically; the glow band slides and tilts so the bars light up and go dark in waves, like an audio meter under the music.
- **Materials:** The glow is a staircase, not a gradient: hard vertical bars, each one flat colour stepping from a warm deep tone through the accent to violet and black across the frame (about 16 bars), with a smooth fade to black vertically; the glow band slides and tilts so the bars light up and go dark in waves, like an audio meter under the music.
- **Conditions:** gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform; glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style
- **Timing:** Spread 36 f; sweep 150 f; wander 244 f.
- **Use when:** Brand-colour sections; checkout or store panels.
- **Avoid when:** A second multi-hue field in the same film.

### Halftone shading

`tx-halftone-shading` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, sting, feature

A flat hero shape gains volume from a single-colour halftone dot field whose dots swell in the shadow side and shrink toward a slowly moving light.

- **Build:** Over the shape, lay an SVG grid of circles on a 12 px pitch, clipped to the shape (clipPath), in C.ink on paper or C.white on ink. Each dot's radius is 5.5 x E.smooth(clamp(dist(L, dot) / R)) px, with L a light point and R about 0.8 x the shape's diagonal; drop dots under 0.8 px radius so nothing aliases. Move L along a slow arc at under 0.5 px/f so the shading breathes, and reveal the field as a diagonal wave in which each dot grows from 0 to its radius over 12 f on E.out, offset by stagger(i, n, 24) with i ordered by x + y.
- **Timing:** Reveal 36 f (a 24 f diagonal stagger plus 12 f per dot on E.out); light point drift under 0.5 px/f; holds as long as the shape stays the hero.
- **Use when:** Flat marks, icons or objects that need volume without 3D; technical or print-minded brands; alongside other dot-matrix devices.
- **Avoid when:** Shapes under ~200 px, where the dots turn to mush; photographic or 3D scenes; busy UI behind the shape.

### Halftone, ASCII and dither as the picture's texture

`dv-screen-texture` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Pictures carry a print or screen texture: a grid of glyphs from a brightness ramp sits over the dark areas of images and re-samples irregularly; silhouettes are filled with a fine dot screen; clouds show a halftone in their shadows under a giant translucent wordmark; a light dot grid overlays a defocused photo; small dither pixels sparkle around subjects' edges.

- **Build:** Recipe: a baked halftone or ASCII plate (rendered once from the image), cycled among 3-4 variants for the flicker. Recipe: the figure as a mask over three radial-dot patterns in pure red, green and blue, offset 1-2 px, screen blend on black; halftone radius per cell = r_max x sqrt(1 - luma). Anatomy: Dot pitch about 4 px at 1080p; glyph ramp . : o O 0; re-sample every 2-7 f (a soft flicker). Sound: None. Materials: Up close the halftone figures are printed in phosphor triads: the dot screen breaks into red, green and blue dots at the edges (8 px pitch, 3 px dots) with a grey core; on a mosaic glitch frame a fine dot grid at 25 % sits over the flat blocks like an LED wall. A frosted bar over a halftone sky averages the screen into soft colour (blur larger than the dot pitch).
- **Materials:** Up close the halftone figures are printed in phosphor triads: the dot screen breaks into red, green and blue dots at the edges (8 px pitch, 3 px dots) with a grey core; on a mosaic glitch frame a fine dot grid at 25 % sits over the flat blocks like an LED wall. A frosted bar over a halftone sky averages the screen into soft colour (blur larger than the dot pitch).
- **Timing:** Static per frame or re-sampled every 2-7 f.
- **Use when:** Image-generation, print, editorial or retro-tech films.
- **Avoid when:** Texture on readable type.

### Picture sliced into offset slats

`dv-slat-offset-picture` · texture and finish · accent · energy medium · launch, sting

A blurred figure is cut into 4-6 horizontal bands that are offset vertically by different amounts, so the image reads as a stepped, sliced object, then the offsets settle.

- **Build:** Build: <Slices kind="slats" at x y w h n={5} spread={0.08}>{picture}</Slices> (fx/Slices): 4-6 horizontal slats offset up and down by seeded amounts that settle to flat on E.snapOut (65 f). Anatomy: Bands 150-250 px; offsets decaying 16 -> 1.5 px/f. Sound: Under the hold.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Slices`
- **Timing:** 65 f ease-out.
- **Use when:** Section breaks on a portrait or a picture.
- **Avoid when:** Faces that must be read.

### Rim highlight from a fixed light

`dv-fixed-rim-highlight` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Every container has a 1 px hairline rim that is brightest at one spot, and the bright spot stays put as the container moves: the light source is fixed in the world.

- **Build:** Recipe: a conic highlight on the border whose angle is computed from the card's position against a fixed light point. Anatomy: Rim highlight computed from the container's position relative to a fixed light. Sound: None. Materials: A spectral rim: a black wordmark on a bright gradient carries a 1.5 px rim at about 0.8, warm on the edges facing the light and cool on the opposite edges (two offset text-shadows), and its interiors carry a faint vertical gradient instead of flat black.
- **Materials:** A spectral rim: a black wordmark on a bright gradient carries a 1.5 px rim at about 0.8, warm on the edges facing the light and cool on the opposite edges (two offset text-shadows), and its interiors carry a faint vertical gradient instead of flat black.
- **Conditions:** glass as a material with real frost or refraction, not a default card style; the film's one spectral accent; gradients baked as dithered plates and moved by transform
- **Timing:** Static per shot.
- **Use when:** Floating cards in a soft, airy look.
- **Avoid when:** Glass looks in house films.

### Stipple only in lit ramps

`tx-ramp-masked-stipple` · texture and finish · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, loop

A visible dithered stipple lives only inside lit edges and light falloffs, while the flat stage around them stays perfectly clean.

- **Build:** Bake each lit ramp (a lit edge on a shape, a light pool, a floor falloff) as an RGBA PNG with scripts/dither-gradient.py, then give the element that carries it a child layer of a static seeded noise tile (sigma about 64 levels around mid-grey) masked by that same PNG (`maskImage: url(fx/rim.png)`, `maskSize: '100% 100%'`), blend overlay at opacity 0.08-0.12. The noise sits inside the ramp's own transform so it travels with the light instead of swimming through it, and wherever the ramp's alpha is 0 the stage gets no texture at all. Check it with the x12 stretch from `dither-gradient.py --preview`: stipple inside the ramp, none on the stage.
- **Timing:** Static texture that moves rigidly with its ramp; high-pass sigma about 1.9 code levels in the brightest ramps, 0.5-0.9 in faint falloffs, 0.0 on the flat stage.
- **Use when:** Dark films with lit edges, light pools or soft falloffs that risk banding, where a global grain would dirty a deliberately clean stage.
- **Avoid when:** Films already running global grain (double texture); light stages; hard-edged flat design with no ramps.

### A band of glyphs traces every subject's edge

`dv-ascii-edge-halo` · texture and finish · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

Around every subject of a photo or plate a band of tiny white monospace glyphs hugs the silhouette like a typed outline (the heaviest glyph at the strongest edge, lighter ones further out, dots bleeding inside); it re-samples every frame so it shimmers as the plate moves, and before a cut it flares, wider, heavier and brighter, and the frame breaks into blocks.

- **Build:** The Ascii glyph atlas drawn on a canvas from a downscaled luma of the plate, with an edge magnitude per cell. Anatomy: Cells 13.5 x 14 px at 1080p, fixed to the screen; the glyph picked by edge strength on a blurred luma: over 0.6 a zero, 0.4-0.6 a small o, 0.2-0.4 a colon, 0.1-0.2 a dot, else empty; white at 0.75-0.9; the band sits mostly outside the silhouette (2-4 cells). Flare: threshold 0.4 -> 0.1 and alpha 0.6 -> 1 over 12 f into a pixelate cut. Sound: None of its own; the flare rides the rising whoosh into the hit. Materials: On strong straight edges the glyph follows the edge angle (tall glyphs on vertical edges, round ones on curves).
- **Primitive:** `fx/GlyphField.GlyphField`
- **Materials:** On strong straight edges the glyph follows the edge angle (tall glyphs on vertical edges, round ones on curves).
- **Timing:** Lives for the plate; flare 12 f, then the pixelate.
- **Use when:** Generated imagery, vision and generation products; plates that need a signature texture.
- **Avoid when:** UI shots; small subjects.

### Intersecting ring field

`tx-ring-field` · texture and finish · signature · energy medium · launch, loop, sting

Above and below a centred band of type, families of huge overlapping ellipse outlines rotate slowly in opposite directions and whip on every copy swap, giving the words an ownable abstract environment.

- **Build:** One full-frame SVG holds two groups of 6-8 ellipses (rx about 47% of frame width, ry about 32% of frame height, centred just above and just below the text band), each a crisp 2 px stroke in one hue whose opacity steps from 0.6 on the outer ring to 0.15 nearest the band. Rotate the groups in opposite directions, angle = +-(0.2 x f + 14 x the sum over swap cues s_k of prog(f, s_k, s_k + 12, E.smooth)), so each copy swap adds a 14-degree whip, and swap the text hard on each whip's peak frame (s_k + 6) so the motion masks the change. The text stays static at the band's centre; the rings' fastest edges (~50 px/f at the whip peak) get the blur pass.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Drop the soft-lit two-hue gradient strokes, the inner blur and the screen blend: every ring is a crisp 2 px stroke in one neutral (white at 15-60% on ink), normal blend, with depth carried by per-ring opacity alone. Keep the rings out of the accent so the accent keeps its one meaning. The full look relies on glow, gradient; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** Drift 0.2 degrees/f between swaps; whip +12-16 degrees over 12 f on E.smooth (peak ~3 degrees/f, ~50 px/f at the outer rim); copy swaps every 60-120 f on the whip's peak frame.
- **Use when:** Type-led launch cards or a statement sequence on a dark stage that needs a signature environment and a motivated way to change copy without cuts.
- **Avoid when:** UI demos, where it competes with the product; light stages, where 2 px rings vanish; more than ~4 s of pure ambience.

### Locked-state mosaic

`tx-locked-mosaic` · texture and finish · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

Withheld content shows as pixelated, desaturated, darkened art with a lock glyph and thin light lines sliding across it, until an unlock snaps it to clean full-tone art.

- **Build:** Pre-render each card's art at 1/40 of its width (blocks about 2.5% of the card width), show it upscaled with `imageRendering: 'pixelated'` and `filter: saturate(0) brightness(0.3)`, and over it 2-3 slightly curved strokes (1.5-2 px, white at 30%) translating linearly along the card at 2-4 px/f, clipped to the card, with a 32-40 px line lock glyph at centre and no caption. Unlock: the strokes brighten to 60% over the 12 f before it, then the art dips from brightness 0.3 to 0.18 over 4 f on E.smooth while the shackle rotates open on SPR.firm; on the next frame swap to the full-resolution art at brightness 1.12 easing to 1.0 over 10 f on E.out, and fade glyph and strokes over 10 f on E.smooth. In a run of cards make each later unlock about 25% faster.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Replace the soft, screen-blended gaussian light ribbons with crisp 1.5-2 px strokes at 30-60% white, and keep the unlock's brightness overshoot inside the card: no burst or rays past its edge. The full look relies on glow; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Pixel.Pixelate`, `fx/Stepped.Stepped`
- **Timing:** Locked state 54-108 f (the strokes keep moving, so nothing is static); unlock = 12 f brighten, 4 f dip, swap, 10 f settle; repeated unlocks 30-45 f apart, each ~25% quicker.
- **Use when:** Premium, gated or upcoming features; a reveal sequence where concealment builds desire; access or unlock stories.
- **Avoid when:** Products with nothing gated; text content (pixelated text reads as broken); more than one reveal device in the same act.

### Scanline transmutation

`tx-scanline-transmute` · texture and finish · signature · energy medium · launch, feature, sting

A bright bar sweeps down a hero object: above the bar the object has already become its digital form, a dot-matrix disc with a crisp rim, while below it the original solid object remains.

- **Build:** Stack two copies of the object in one container: the solid version and a dot-matrix version (an SVG <pattern> of 5 px-radius circles on a 16 px pitch, clipped to the object's outline, plus a 2 px rim stroke). Drive one value y (percent of the object's height) and clip the dot layer with `clipPath: inset(0 0 ${100 - y}% 0)` and the solid layer with `inset(${y}% 0 0 0)`; draw the bar as a hard-edged rect centred on y, 3-4% of the frame height thick, clipped to the object's column so it enters already moving from 8% above the object. Chain three segments: -8% to 45% over f0-11 on E.linear, 45% to 50% over f11-17 on E.linear (a near-hold that catches on the object's symbol), 50% to 100% over f17-34 on E.glide; the fast segments run 20-40 px/f and get the blur pass. Put a whoosh apex on the third segment's velocity peak and a snap on f34.
- **Ban-safe variant (the default):** Keep the sweep but drop the bloom and the tint: a flat, hard-edged bar 12-24 px thick in white or the accent (or a 2 px hairline with a 10% tint band 40 px behind it), dots in white or the accent, never violet, and nothing lit outside the object's outline. The full look relies on glow, purple; use it only when the brand supplies that look.
- **Timing:** 34 f in all: 11 f fast (20-30 px/f at 1080p), a 6 f near-hold at ~4-6 px/f on the symbol, 17 f on E.glide to rest; bar 36-40 px; the transformed object then holds 24-40 f with a drift under 1 px/f.
- **Use when:** One hero transformation per film: an object becoming its private, digital, encrypted or connected form; the moment the concept turns.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film; ordinary UI state changes; objects under ~25% of frame height, where the dot pitch cannot read.

### Symbol string tiles the frame and resolves into an ASCII object

`dv-ascii-globe-resolve` · texture and finish · signature · energy high · launch, sting

A short string of symbols repeats in a grid that fills the panel, turns into character columns, and resolves into a flickering ASCII-dither globe.

- **Build:** Build: <AsciiField at x y w h src color> (fx/Ascii): the symbol string tiles the panel, turns into seeded character columns (from 22 f), the picture resolves through a dark-to-light glyph ramp (from 44 f, settled by 63) and flickers like a dither: about 6 % of the cells swap to a ramp neighbour every 3-8 f. Anatomy: Grid of characters; columns; luminance mapped to a glyph ramp; style flicker every 1-3 f. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Ascii.AsciiField`
- **Timing:** Settle 63 f; flicker every 3-8 f at 60 fps.
- **Use when:** A film about the web, data or the world; a title reveal from code.
- **Avoid when:** Without a plate to convert.

### Wireframe-to-product scan

`tx-wireframe-scan-build` · texture and finish · signature · energy medium · launch, feature

A thin accent line sweeps across a UI card: ahead of it the card is still a wireframe of outlines and skeleton bars, behind it the finished product is already there.

- **Build:** Render the component twice in one container: the real UI, and a wire version of the same component (backgrounds transparent, every box a 1.5 px C.line outline, text replaced by rounded bars at the measured text width and 40% opacity, icons as outlined circles). Drive x from -4% to 100% of the card width with prog(f, s, s + 44, E.smooth) and, clamped to 0-100, clip the real layer with `inset(0 ${100 - x}% 0 0)` and the wire layer with `inset(0 0 0 ${x}%)`, and draw a 2 px C.accent line at x reaching 24 px past the card's top and bottom, with no glow. Add a soft swell event across the sweep and a snap as the line leaves the card, then fade the line over 10 f on E.smooth.
- **Timing:** Sweep 40-48 f on E.smooth across a 600-900 px card (edge peak ~40-58 px/f; the UI itself never moves); line fade 10 f; the finished card then holds at least 30 f under a 0.5-1.5 px/f camera drift.
- **Use when:** Idea-to-product, design-to-code, generation or build stories; the first appearance of the hero UI.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film; UI too sparse to read as a wireframe; a film that already uses another scan device such as scanline transmutation.
